generation.turnaroundSheet: codex-image (Codex CLI image_gen), 16:9 four-view product turnaround reference sheet on a pure white seamless background
generation.sheetCrop: scripts/turnaround_crop.mjs — gutter-detected crop into 4 single-view PNGs
generation.mesh: Higgsfield generate_3d, model multi_image_to_3d, 4 views role=image, should_texture=true, enable_pbr=true, should_remesh=true, topology=triangle, target_polycount=30000, symmetry_mode=auto, rigging/animation disabled

source.postProcessing: npx @gltf-transform/cli resize --width 1024 --height 1024; scripts/fit_glb.py per-axis fit (capped at 10% anisotropy), footprint centred and base placed at y=0
source.title: Potted fiddle-leaf fig
source.description: Sculptural potted fiddle-leaf fig: two slender bare woody trunks carrying large broad violin-shaped leaves, in a matte stoneware planter.
source.artDirection: Warm Japandi: solid oak with fine open grain, matte finish, gently chamfered edges; the plant in a matte stoneware pot.

requestedSizeCm.note: Rough target for the demo catalogue. The recorded widthCm/depthCm/heightCm above are measured from the GLB and take precedence.

measured.method: backend/api/glb.py measure(), read back from the fitted GLB

knownLimitations: No real product: geometry, texture and proportions come from an AI-generated turnaround sheet, not from a grower's or manufacturer's model. matchType is generic_visual_proxy; do not present it as a specific purchasable item.
price_cents in the batch manifest is invented for the demo and has no vendor behind it.
The per-axis fit is capped at 10% anisotropy: measured 67.8 x 68.0 x 152.2 cm against a requested rough 70 x 70 x 150 cm. The dimensions recorded here are the measured ones.

Foliage is solid geometry, not alpha-cut cards: leaves are thick slabs with rounded edges rather than thin blades, and leaf-to-stalk joins are blobby at close range. It is built to read correctly at room scale, not in close-up.

Verified by rendering the GLB in three.js from the front and rear: the leaves stayed individually separated on visible trunks and did NOT fuse into a single green mass, which is the usual failure for plants in image-to-3D.
The planter reads as a near-white light grey rather than the warm oatmeal speckle described in the prompt.
The bounding box spans the leaf canopy, so its footprint is much wider than the pot; any placement or collision logic keyed to the footprint will reserve more floor than the pot physically occupies.
